text:
Avery: Hey, new hire here — just got my MBP M2. Trying to do a clean OS install before enrolling in MDM but can't boot external USB. Trying to reinstall from recovery, but FileVault is enabled and `fdesetup` needs admin. Is there a standard one-time admin flow or can IT disable FV remotely?

Karen (IT): Welcome! We usually either create a temp admin account or schedule a quick remote session. Can you paste output of `fdesetup status`?

Avery: Sure — here's what I ran in Recovery Terminal:
```
$ fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Recovery Key: Present
```
Also tried Startup Options — it hangs on "Verifying" when booting from USB.

Mike (IT): On M1/M2 devices booting external can be blocked by Startup Security settings. If it's company device assigned via ABM, we can revive using Apple Configurator, but easiest: we can create a temp local admin so you can run `fdesetup disable` before reinstall. Do you want remote screenshare or a temporary account?

Avery: Temp account would be great — I'm available in 30 mins.

Karen (IT): Created temp account: username `rdw-temp-avery`, password `Redwood!2026`. Expires in 4 hours and will be audited. Use it to run:
```
sudo fdesetup disable
sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install --all
```
After reinstall, sign into Okta and run the MDM enrollment link from the onboarding email.

Avery: Thanks — I was able to disable FileVault and reinstall. Ran `fdesetup status` again:
```
FileVault is Off
```
Enrolled in MDM and Okta SSO worked.

Sophia: Welcome aboard! :tada:

Avery: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. Leaving note: if your device shows "Verifying" on external boot, reach out to IT; Apple Startup Security often blocks externals unless set via ABM.

Karen (IT): Closing the loop — temp account revoked. If you hit any policy prompts during enrollment ping #new-hires or IT directly.
